core_obligations: Reduce statement (1) to degree one by dimension shifting (proof lines 8989-8990): it suffices to show that H^1(G, M) is torsion for every G-module M.

Represent a class in H^1(G, M) by an invariant element of N (proof lines 8991-8994): take 0 -> M -> I -> N -> 0 with I injective, so that every element of H^1(G, M) is the image of some y in N^G, and lift y to x in I.

Produce an integer killing that class (proof lines 8995-8999): the stabiliser U of x is open, hence of finite index r; choosing representatives g_1, ..., g_r of G/U, the sum of the g_i(x) is G-invariant and maps to ry, so r annihilates the class in H^1(G, M).
Deduce statement (2) (proof lines 8999-9000): if M is a Q-vector space then H^i(G, M) is a Q-vector space as well, and by (1) it is torsion in positive degrees, hence zero.
proof_roadmap: Dimension shift to reduce (1) to H^1(G, M) torsion.
Embed M into an injective I with quotient N, and represent a class in H^1(G, M) as the image of y in N^G.
Lift y to x in I; the stabiliser U of x is open of finite index r.
Sum the translates of x over a set of representatives of G/U to get an invariant element mapping to ry, so r kills the class.
For (2), a Q-vector space that is torsion is zero.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the cohomology of a profinite group in positive degrees: it is torsion, and it vanishes on Q-vector spaces (statement lines 8978-8986). The substantive step is the degree-one computation (proof lines 8989-8999): one represents a class in H^1(G, M) by an invariant element y of the quotient N of an injective I, lifts y to x in I, and then uses that the stabiliser U of x is open, hence of finite index r, so that the sum of the translates of x over representatives of G/U is invariant and maps to ry. The non-formal point is exactly this use of openness of the stabiliser in the profinite topology to manufacture the killing integer. The claim is H2: one explicit construction after a standard dimension-shifting reduction.
